blogs.title: When Angioedema Isn't: The 'Pseudo-Angioedema' of Dermatomyositis
blogs.description: This post explores the diagnostic pitfall of mistaking inflammatory myopathy for allergic or bradykinin-mediated angioedema. We will analyze the pathophysiology behind 'pseudo-angioedema' in dermatomyositis—where subcutaneous edema results from severe muscle inflammation and capillary leak rather than mast cell degranulation. Key teaching points include recognizing red flags that argue against true angioedema (e.g., lack of response to standard therapies, concurrent proximal weakness, elevated CRP without fever) and understanding why a simple CK level should be part of the workup for unexplained neck swelling.

blogs.title: Beyond Gottron's Papules: Subtle Cutaneous Clues in Seronegative-Looking Myositis
blogs.description: Classic dermatomyositis presents with heliotrope rashes and Gottron's papules, but this case highlights a patient lacking these hallmark signs yet suffering from severe disease. This article focuses on the importance of meticulous physical examination, specifically looking for 'minor' cutaneous markers like periungual telangiectasias, nailfold capillary changes (avascular areas/microhemorrhages), and the holster sign. We will discuss how these subtle findings, often missed in the chaotic ED environment, can trigger the correct diagnostic pathway before irreversible muscle damage occurs.

blogs.title: The Anti-SAE1 Phenotype: Dysphagia, Edema, and Malignancy Risk
blogs.description: Not all myositis antibodies create the same clinical picture. This post dives deep into the specific phenotype associated with anti-SAE1 antibodies, characterized by a higher prevalence of severe dysphagia, cutaneous ulceration/edema, and interstitial lung disease compared to other subsets. We will review current literature regarding the malignancy risk associated with anti-SAE1 (approx. 18%) and outline a robust cancer screening strategy for high-risk inflammatory myopathy patients, balancing aggressive surveillance with resource stewardship.

blogs.title: Airway Anxiety vs. Muscle Failure: Managing Dysphagia and Aspiration in Acute Myositis
blogs.description: While emergency providers often fear immediate airway obstruction in patients with neck swelling, this case illustrates that the primary threat in dermatomyositis is often profound bulbar weakness leading to silent aspiration and pneumonia. This post discusses the management tension between securing an artificial airway versus managing secretion clearance and nutrition in patients with severe pharyngeal dysphagia. We will cover indications for video fluoroscopic swallowing studies, the role of NG tubes versus early PEG placement, and strategies to prevent aspiration pneumonitis in the acute phase.

blogs.title: Escalation Therapy: Navigating Steroid-Sparing Agents in Severe Dermatomyositis
blogs.description: High-dose steroids are the cornerstone of initial therapy, but cases with massive CK elevation (>10,000 U/L) and organ-threatening involvement (dysphagia, ILD) often require rapid escalation. This post analyzes the rationale behind choosing specific second-line agents like IVIG, Rituximab, and Mycophenolate Mofetil over traditional options like Methotrexate (particularly in the context of lung involvement). We will break down the mechanism of action for these biologics in myositis and discuss practical considerations for dosing, monitoring, and infection prophylaxis during intense immunosuppression.
